newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-STEVENS'S FIRST ROYAL ASCOT WIN MARRED BY BAN.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-STEVENS'S FIRST ROYAL ASCOT WIN MARRED BY BAN.

text.p: Leading American jockey Gary Stevens achieved a lifelong ambition on Friday when he rode the first Royal Ascot winner of his distinguished career and his first in Britain.

But the joy was shortlived. In the next race he arrived late on the scene on the heavily backed favourite, got beaten a neck by a 25-1 apprentice-ridden outsider and was then handed a two-day ban for improper use of the whip.
The suspension starts on June 29 and it appeared at first Stevens would have to miss two big U.S. races.

The Ascot stewards ruled that Stevens had used his whip excessively on Danetime in the Wokingham Stakes, one of the top sprint handicaps of the year. Danetime had been backed down from 12-1 to 7-1 favourite.
Ron Anderson, Stevens's agent, said: "This ban could not have started on a worse day as he is due to ride Gentleman in the Hollywood Gold Cup and Donna Viola in the Beverley Hill Stakes.
"We are examining appeal procedures. In the U.S. this type of ban does not apply on days with grade one races."
Malcolm Wallace, the British Jockey Club's director of rules, said: "If the Americans wish to allow Gary Stevens to ride on June 29 there will be no objections from us."

Ironically, Stevens had been at his brilliant best 40 minutes earlier in the big race of the final day of the four-day meeting, forcing 6-1 chance Predappio back into the lead to land the valuable Hardwicke Stakes from Breeders' Cup Turf winner Pilsudski, the 2-1 favourite ridden by Michael Kinane.
The 34-year-old American narrowly missed out on this year's U.S. Triple Crown when he was beaten on Silver Charm in the Belmont Stakes but his victory on Friday was a handsome compensation.

Stevens, with over 4,000 career wins to his credit, had endured two frustrating second places, a third and eight unplaced rides earlier in the meeting and it was beginning to look as if he might return home empty-handed.
But with Frankie Dettori suspended for the final day's action following a riding offence at Epsom, Stevens was snapped up for the mount on Predappio, a much-improved colt.
Stevens said: "That was something special, right up there with my (three Kentucky) Derbys.
"It would have been a fun week but I would have gone home disappointed had I not been fortunate enough to win a race.
"Fortunately, I found a horse with a bigger heart than I've got, I think. I thought I was beaten half a furlong (100 metres) out but this horse dug down. He found something else."
Predappio had led the classy 10-strong field into the straight but Pilsudski was looming ominously on his oustide.
Pilsudski went a neck clear with 100 metres to travel but Predappio found a final surge to land the spoils by half a length.
The winner on the second rain-soaked day in succession was another for the Godolphin team of Sheikh Mohammed, back in form after a miserable run earlier in the season.
Godolphin racing manager Simon Crisford said: "Predappio will be in everything. We will take on the best because that's what he deserves."
The first race of the day, the Windsor Castle Stakes, had also gone to Godolphin with Richard Hills partnering Asfurah to a battling neck victory.
Despite not riding on Friday, Dettori ended top Royal Ascot jockey with four winners and four seconds.
